blocks.x: Applied AI & GenAI for Industrial Equipment & Machinery: what the sector's controls demand, what we build on the platform rails, and the outcomes written into the engagement.

Equipment makers pivot to outcome businesses: connected machines, service contracts and uptime guarantees replace box sales. The pivot is an engineering program — fleet connectivity, service intelligence and outcome pricing — built once, monetized for decades.

items: Failure data accumulates without models; warranty and design loops closed by anecdote.
Machines in the field lack telemetry; service is reactive and parts planning blind.

Governance inherits the sector frame — EU Machinery Regulation/CRA among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Align AI to P&L lines and risk mandates — a sequenced portfolio, not a pile of pilots.

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Manufacturing & Industrial level this capability reads as: multivariate telemetry models flagging drift before scrap is produced (scrap and rework cost down 15-25%). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

This capability runs on the cadence set out below; the rhythm is fixed, the scope is signed. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
